stories.summary: Trying to decide between a couple of closely ranked players this week? Eric Karabell's rankings are here to help.
stories.body:
Welcome to Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season and our weekly PPR fantasy football superflex rankings. We know many of you compete in superflex formats that invite/covet second quarterbacks in starting lineups, and these rankings account for that. It might look odd to see the lowest-ranked fantasy passers ahead of typical RB2 and WR2 options, but the potential scoring impact demands it.

If your league is a standard flex, note that rankings without QBs appear below the superflex rankings. However you prefer to play, good luck this week!

Standard flex rankings (RBs, WRs, TEs only)

stories.headline: Fantasy baseball news and notes: Carroll ready for playoff push and more for Friday
stories.summary: All of the important fantasy spin and actionable takeaways resulting from the latest baseball news.
stories.body:
Everything that happens in and around MLB has some additional context when viewed from a fantasy baseball perspective. From lineup changes to minor league call-ups to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy baseball.

Our fantasy baseball buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around MLB.

Key links: RP depth chart | Player Rater | Scoring leaders

10-day pitching forecaster | 10-day hitting forecaster

Sept. 11: Friday's Forecaster findings
By Tristan H. Cockcroft

Over the next 10 days of play, we're almost certain to see our first significant postseason berths clinched. The Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers are virtual locks to assure themselves playoff berths (as a starting point) during the Sept. 11-13 weekend and several teams are within reach of celebrating during the upcoming week.

The Brewers (magic number of 5) and Los Angeles Dodgers (6) can clinch their respective divisions, and the New York Yankees (4), Dodgers (5), Atlanta Braves (8) and Boston Red Sox (9) can clinch wild-card spots, all of which seem likely to occur during fantasy's Week 24. From a player motivation standpoint, fantasy managers should prefer players from games with something on the line, and it's not uncommon for a team clinching some type of postseason berth or seeding to rest veteran players afterward, often in the game immediately following that happening.
The AL Central-leading Chicago White Sox visit the Cleveland Guardians, 1.5 games back in the division, for three games at Progressive Field from Monday through Wednesday.
The Toronto Blue Jays and Texas Rangers -- 1 and 2 games back in the AL wild-card race, respectively -- play three games at Globe Life Field from Friday through Sunday.
The Arizona Diamondbacks, 0.5 games back in the NL wild-card race, visit the Yankees, 3 games back in the AL East, from Friday through Sunday.
Fantasy managers could get boosts with the prospective returns of two injured hitters: Willson Contreras (hamstring) is on a minor league rehab stint and seems likely to be activated either at the start of or in advance of Boston's Week 24 road trip to Texas and Tampa Bay. Shea Langeliers (knee), once believed to be done for the season, is instead now on a minor league rehab stint and might begin to see some work as DH for the Athletics at some point during Week 24.
The Colorado Rockies play the entire week at Coors Field in one of only two weeks all season where they're scheduled for seven games there, and one of just four weeks played entirely at Coors. The Rockies do face a pair of talented pitching staffs in the San Diego Padres (4 games, Monday through Thursday) and Seattle Mariners (3, Friday through Sunday), but Coors' hitter-friendly confines nevertheless tilt things in favor of Rockies hitters in those matchups. Additionally, visiting Padres and Mariners hitters get to capitalize against Rockies pitching, which has baseball's worst ERA (5.50).

For the full Week 24 Forecaster, you can find all ratings, scheduling quirks and SP projections right here.

Sept. 11: Friday's news to know
By Todd Zola

After a light Thursday, everyone is in action today, with the Chicago Cubs and Pittsburgh Pirates kicking things off at 2:20 p.m. ET with a Wrigley Field matinee.

Corbin Carroll is expected to return to the Arizona Diamondbacks tonight. He missed the club's last two games due to a sore lower back. He went for an MRI on yesterday's off day, and it came back negative. Carroll's return is timely, with the Diamondbacks opening a series with the Texas Rangers only one-half game behind the San Diego Padres for the last NL wild-card spot.
Brandon Marsh exited Thursday afternoon's game after fouling a ball off his foot in the eighth inning. The Philadelphia Phillies open an important road series with the Atlanta Braves tonight and Marsh's status is uncertain. The Phillies are four games behind the Braves for the NL East lead.
The Washington Nationals placed Nasim Nunez on the bereavement list. He's expected to miss this weekend's home set with the Los Angeles Angels. Nunez leads the majors with 46 stolen bases.
The St. Louis Cardinals are optimistic that Masyn Winn will return to the lineup tonight when they entertain the Chicago White Sox. The slick-fielding shortstop was activated from the IL on Tuesday after recovering from a broken left thumb, but he was unable to play Wednesday because of residual soreness. After yesterday's off day, Winn is now expected to be ready to take the field.

Be sure to check out the latest fantasy lineup advice as well as the MLB betting tips for Friday.

Sept. 10: Thursday's news to know

By Todd Zola

It's a light day in MLB, with only five games on the schedule. The Atlanta Braves and Tampa Bay Rays get things started at Truist Field at 12:15 p.m. ET. Two more afternoon games follow, then two night games.

Shohei Ohtani missed his second straight game last night and he's appeared only once in the Los Angeles Dodgers' last seven contests. The two-way star is nursing a sore knee and biceps. The club had hesitated to place him on the 15-day IL, but finally relented last night.
To replace Ohtani, the Dodgers are calling up Josue De Paula from Double-A Tulsa, who will join the team for Friday's matchup with the Miami Marlins. De Paula is No. 10 overall in Kiley McDaniel's updated 2026 MLB top 100 prospect rankings. The 21-year-old outfielder hit .303/.401/.547 with 27 homers and 31 steals in 124 games for the Drillers.
The New York Yankees will be without 2B Jazz Chisholm Jr. for at least 10 days and possibly the rest of the regular season after placing him on the 10-day IL. He sprained his right thumb sliding into second base Tuesday night. The club will reportedly recall Anthony Volpe from Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre. Along with Jose Caballero, Volpe is an option to fill in at second.
Hagen Smith is set to make his first MLB start tonight when the Chicago White Sox entertain the Pittsburgh Pirates. He is ranked No. 4 in McDaniel's updated prospect rankings. The 23-year-old left-hander has made 10 big league appearances out of the bullpen, posting a pristine 0.56 ERA and an 0.94 WHIP over 16 innings. He's averaged 34 pitches over his last four outings, so Smith won't likely pitch deep into the game.

stories.headline: 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup: Team USA and semifinal preview
stories.summary: The FIBA Women's World Cup semifinal matchups are set. How does each team stack up going into Saturday's games?
stories.body:
BERLIN -- The semifinals of the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup are set, albeit with relatively few surprises.

The United State and France continued their undefeated runs with convincing wins over Hungary and China, respectively, in the quarterfinals. In the other games Thursday, Spain pounced on short-handed Australia, and host nation Germany -- playing in only its second World Cup -- upset reigning EuroBasket champ Belgium.

The host country has now made the semifinals in each of the past six World Cups, medaling in half those instances. Play will resume Saturday with the semifinals, followed by the medal rounds on Sunday.

The U.S. women are aiming for their fifth consecutive World Cup gold and 12th overall; the program has lost only one game at a major international tournament -- the World Cup and Olympics -- since 1994.

But the United States hasn't looked entirely invincible in this tournament -- it hasn't helped to be without A'ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum -- and it has never been more clear that the gap between the Americans and the rest of the world is rapidly closing.

Here's what you need to know about the last four teams standing. The number in parenthesis reflects the team's current FIBA ranking (last updated on April 1).

Germany (11) vs. France (2)

10:30 a.m. ET Saturday

Current Germany WNBA players:

F Frieda Buhner, Portland Fire

G Leonie Fiebich, New York Liberty

C Luisa Geiselsoder, Portland Fire

F Nyara Sabally, Toronto Tempo

Current France WNBA players:

G Pauline Astier, New York Liberty

F Valeriane Ayayi, Phoenix Mercury

G Marine Johannes, New York Liberty

G Leila Lacan, Connecticut Sun

G Carla Leite, Portland Fire

C Dominique Malonga, Seattle Storm

F Janelle Salaun, Golden State Valkyries

G Gabby Williams, Golden State Valkyries

How do they match up:

This will be a matchup of two teams with something to prove. After getting tantalizingly close to beating the U.S. for the gold at the 2024 Olympics, France has not shied from saying it's going for it all in Berlin.

"All we care about is winning," Malonga said after France beat China. "The French national team has been known for years for like second place or semifinals, never all the way, even in EuroBasket, until now -- I feel like we have to do it. We have to make it happen."

Players credited Golden State Valkyries star Williams for helping change the culture of the French national team to one of high standards, accountability and confidence. Players aren't just happy to be there, but instead want to win and make history as perhaps the greatest team to ever suit up for France.

France is certainly playing like a squad that could win gold, beating teams by an average of 39 points. Les Bleues are known for their defensive identity, but the group has shined offensively this World Cup, averaging 98.8 points on 53.3% shooting, including a blistering 45.7% from the 3-point arc.

Germany, meanwhile, is enjoying its best-ever finish in either of the two major international tournaments, all while being without star Satou Sabally and having to bounce back from a crushing 30-point rout to Spain to open the tournament.

In fact, Germany's quarterfinal upset over Belgium might already be the best day in the history of its women's team, multiple players said. Coach Olaf Lange said he was a little speechless with how well his team played, with six players scoring in double figures and stars Fiebich (17 points, 10 rebounds) and Nyara Sabally (16 points, 12 rebounds) finishing with double-doubles.

Thursday's result alone ensures the 2026 World Cup is a success for Germany, but it has more to compete for. Multiple players were asked about the game being a rematch of the quarterfinals from the Paris Olympics -- a 84-71 France victory -- and the pain of that loss was clearly still fresh even two years later.

The Germans once more will be considered the underdogs against France but will receive a major boost from their fans, who have filled Uber Arena in droves throughout the tournament, as they look to keep making history on home soil.

United States (1) vs. Spain (6)
2 p.m. ET Saturday

Current USA WNBA players:

F/C Aliyah Boston, Indiana Fever

G Paige Bueckers, Dallas Wings

G Sonia Citron, Washington Mystics

G Caitlin Clark, Indiana Fever

F Napheesa Collier, Minnesota Lynx

F/G Kahleah Copper, Phoenix Mercury

G Chelsea Gray, Las Vegas Aces

G Rhyne Howard, Atlanta Dream

F Kiki Iriafen, Washington Mystics

F Angel Reese, Atlanta Dream

F Breanna Stewart, New York Liberty

G Jackie Young, Las Vegas Aces

Current Spain WNBA players:

G Elena Buenavida, Minnesota Lynx (developmental player)

C Raquel Carrera, New York Liberty

F Maria Conde, Toronto Tempo

C Megan DiLeo, Portland Fire

C Awa Fam, Seattle Storm

G Alicia Florez, Washington Mystics

How do they match up:

On Thursday, the U.S. took another step toward making its group phase scare against Italy look like an anomaly, demolishing Hungary by 52 points and setting or flirting with a litany of records.

One positive development from the quarterfinal was the way Collier came out aggressive and productive from the jump, scoring 10 first-quarter points and 19 on the game -- notably, that's her senior team personal best in scoring (besting the 12 points she scored Monday against Czechia).

The Lynx star is still working her way back from a long rehab process following double ankle surgery this offseason, but the more she plays the way she has in the past two games, the better for the Americans. She and Young -- the only U.S. player to reach double figures each game -- are now the top scorers for the Americans this tournament.

"I think just moving a lot without the ball," Collier said of how she found success Thursday. "Making sure I'm super active, getting second-chance opportunities, cutting, just playing my normal game a little bit more."

Across the board, the team felt this was its best performance of the World Cup, not only because of what it accomplished offensively but because of how it started on defense. There was also a recognition that now, 10 or so days into the tournament, the chemistry is starting to come together and players are learning how to play alongside each other even more.

All of that bodes well going into the final two days of games. That said, neither Hungary nor Czechia were the toughest of tests for the U.S. Spain -- which nearly took home EuroBasket gold the past two tournaments -- should be much stiffer competition. If over the weekend things get mucked up offensively, or the U.S. finds itself struggling more generally, all eyes will be on how the team learned from the Italy experience in how to work through adversity, both in which individuals step up and how the group comes together.

Spain, which features a litany of current and former WNBA players, had a perplexing loss to Mali on the second day of its group phase, but it features an intriguing mix of experienced vets and young talent that've propelled it back to within reach of a fourth medal in the past five World Cups.

The unit took down Australia with a well-rounded effort that included six players scoring at least nine points. But to knock off the Americans, it feels as if Spain will need to have breakout games from its 20-year-old pair of Iyana Martin and Fam, the former a Portland Fire first-round draft pick and the latter a Seattle Storm rookie.

The Madring is a hybrid between a street circuit and a purpose-built track, using a mixture of public roads and private land around the IFEMA Madrid exhibition centre.

The circuit is 5.416km long and features 22 corners. Sunday's race will take place over 57 laps.

Formula 1 is returning to Madrid for the first time since 1981, when the Spanish Grand Prix was held at Jarama, around 30 kilometres north of the city.

Mercedes' George Russell said ahead of the weekend: "I would put it, arguably, as the most risky circuit of the whole calendar, because you have real high-speed corners, sort of Jeddah-esque. The walls are very close. There's no margin for error.

"But then, you have other corners that are quite like Baku, where you're coming from a high speed into a slow braking zone. You're braking and turning at the same time.

"So, locking tyres is going to be easy. If you're not coping, you'll be straight in the wall.

"I think it's going to be really challenging for us as drivers. The race is going to be challenging to overtake. So, on the whole, it's not an easy one."

Alpine's Pierre Gasly added: "I must say it's exciting, but at the same time I think it's going to be quite a disruptive weekend, how easy it will be to have a crash."

stories.headline: Fenerbahçe coach Kartal misses training despite club blocking resignation
stories.summary: Fenerbahçe coach Ismail Kartal announced his shock resignation after the 1-1 draw against Roma, but club president Aziz Yildirim said the coach remains in his position.
stories.body:
Fenerbahce coach Ismail Kartal failed to appear at training on Friday, Turkish media reports said, a day after he announced he was stepping down following a draw against Roma in a Champions League game but the club refused to accept his resignation.

Kartal stunned a postmatch news conference following the 1-1 draw against Roma by announcing his intention to leave the club, a move that club president Aziz Yıldırım swiftly rejected.

"I have stepped down tonight," Kartal said. "I made this decision to clear the way for my club. I am resigning with the intention of never returning."

Kartal, who returned to the Istanbul side in June 2026 for his fourth stint, thanked the club for its support and congratulated his players on a match "we could have won," before adding that "from now on, to help Fenerbahçe, my footballers, I have resigned from my position, on the condition of never returning."

The announcement caught club officials entirely off guard, prompting Yıldırım to address the media minutes later to override the manager's decision.

"İsmail Kartal remains in charge. The club must support our coach. As long as I remain president, Kartal is the Fenerbahçe coach," Yıldırım said.

"There is no need for İsmail Kartal to say he will continue. I am his superior; I tell him, 'You will continue,' and that's that."

Playing in front of a sold-out Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium, Fenerbahçe marked their return to Europe's top-tier competition for the first time since the 2008-09 campaign.

Roma opened the scoring when Bryan Cristante capitalized with a low shot from outside the box in the 39th minute. Fenerbahçe responded early in the second half when left back Archie Brown expertly flicked the ball over the goalkeeper to equalize in the 48th minute.

Fenerbahçe will return to action on Monday to face Gaziantep FK in the Turkish Super Lig.

Information from the Associated Press contributed to this report.

Fiala had 18 goals and 22 assists in 56 games for the Kings last season. stories.headline: What We Learned: Knights never give up; Bennett's selections puzzled
stories.summary: The Newcastle Knights have beaten South Sydney at Allianz Stadium, advancing to the second week of the final. Here's what we learned from the game.
stories.body:
The Newcastle Knights have beaten South Sydney at Allianz Stadium, advancing to the second week of the finals, sending the Rabbitohs crashing out of what was a promising season.

Here are three things we learned from the game:

Knights never stop fighting

Suspensions, injuries, away from home - don't worry about any of it. Very few gave Newcastle a shot in this one but right from the jump they were more physical, more enthusiastic and took their chances. It wasn't a typical Knights showing because while they did score a long-range try, they had a mountain of ball in territory and won this via attrition rather than dazzling football.

Both first half tries came off kicks, but it was being in good attacking positions to end their sets which allowed that to happen. All week, a lot of people, including me, thought if they'd win it would be by throwing a few counter punches and defending gamely. They didn't really need to.

They were meant to be the team on the back foot, with a forward pack devoid of stars They dominated in yardage, robbed Souths of good ball, and suffocated their way to victory. It's so against type for them it's hard to really believe, but as hard-earned a win as the Knights have got all year. Bring on week two.

Bennett's selection puzzlers finally catch up

The loudest cheer from the Souths fans at the Sydney Football Stadium didn't come at kick off, or even when Campbell Graham scored - rather, it was Jye Gray being subbed on to the field in the second half that got the punters up and about.

Gray is beloved by Rabbitohs supporters and with good reason; he was one of the few bright sparks in an awful 2025 season and has made stuff happen every time he's on the field in 2026.

However, a few weeks' ago, coach Wayne Bennett made the decision to bench Gray in favour of Matt Dufty, who's return to the NRL after several years in the wilderness has been a great story in its own right - but it's a decision that's puzzled plenty, including me. Dufty was poor in kick defence for each of the opening two tries and threw a late intercept to stop any hopes of a comeback. It was a selection misfire.

Similarly, after Ashton Ward was ruled out for the season it was assumed that Jamie Humphreys would be the halfback the rest of the way. Instead it was Bud Sullivan who Bennett went with, and his decision making on Friday night was pretty rough for the most part.

Still, both Sullivan and Dufty have had great moments at times. The other and much more puzzling situation has been the refusal to play hooker Peter Mamouzelos, the most creative nine at the club and best foil to Brandon Smith. Every single Souths fan I've spoken to is baffled as to why Mamouzelos can't get into the team, particularly when the players who are getting minutes at hooker instead of him aren't hookers by trade. It makes no sense.

All of this is largely moot though because without Cody Walker, Souths weren't going to make any real impact on the finals series, even if they had stolen this one late on. Maybe next year.

Back-row brilliance from Newcastle

Take a bow, Jermaine McEwen and Francis Manuleleua. McEwen especially was superb with his two tries, but it was the edge integrity that allowed the Knights to stay on top in this one. Souths are so deadly on both sides but particularly their left, but for the most part those sweeping raids to the flanks were shut down with ease and that begins with the backrowers.

Again, this wasn't a position where you looked at Newcastle as having an advantage, but they were just better on the night.

We all know about the stars that the Knights have in other areas of the field, many of whom were great tonight. But if they can get this level of production from less-heralded guys, who knows how far they can go?

stories.summary: The Los Angeles Rams' defeat in Week 1 in Melbourne, Australia was a historic low for a preseason Super Bowl champion.
stories.body:
Everything that happens in sports has additional context when viewed from a sports betting perspective. From season-changing injuries to record-setting moments and so much more, the sports news cycle will constantly and significantly affect the sports betting industry.

Sept 11: Rams suffer worst opening loss by preseason Super Bowl favorite in 50 years

by David Purdum

Preseason Super Bowl favorites have lost before, just not as badly as the Los Angeles Rams did Thursday in Melbourne, Australia.

The Rams lost 27-7 to the San Francisco 49ers, becoming the first preseason Super Bowl favorite to lose its opener by 20 or more in the last 50 seasons, according to SportsOddHistory.com. The 1993 Dallas Cowboys lost by 19, and the 2017 New England Patriots and 1987 New York Giants each lost by 15 in their season openers. Both the Cowboys and Patriots would play in the Super Bowl in those seasons, with the Cowboys winning and the Patriots losing, but the Giants failed to make the playoffs.

Los Angeles closed as a 3.5-point favorite over the 49ers and attracted the bulk of the bets and money from bettors. BetMGM reported that 60% of the money bet on the point spread was on the Rams.

The Rams have attracted more than twice as many bets to win the Super Bowl as any other team at DraftKings Sportsbook. They remain the favorites to win the Super Bowl, NFC and NFC West, but their odds dipped from 5-1 to 6-1 after Thursday's loss, and their odds to win the NFC West shifted from -105 to +164.

The 49ers, in turn, improved from +300 to +180 to win the division. The defending-champion Seattle Seahawks moved from +215 to +184 in the tightly-contested NFC West. San Francisco improved from 19-1 to 14-1 to win the Super Bowl at DraftKings.

stories.headline: Team USA scores 108 in rout of Hungary to reach FIBA semis
stories.summary: The U.S. routed Hungary 108-56 to advance to the semifinals of the women's FIBA World Cup and stretched its winning streak in the tournament to 34 games.
stories.body:
BERLIN -- After a scare in the group phase against Italy, Team USA knew it wouldn't be able to play poorly in the knockout rounds of the FIBA World Cup if it wanted to come away with a fifth straight gold medal and 12th overall.

It was only the quarterfinals, but the U.S. responded to that challenge, putting together what the team viewed as its best performance of the tournament with a 108-56 drilling of Hungary. The Americans' 108 points and 31 assists were both records for a World Cup quarterfinal game.

Napheesa Collier led all scorers with 19 points -- a personal best with the senior national team -- followed by 15 from Rhyne Howard and 10 each from Kahleah Copper, Caitlin Clark and Jackie Young.

"We talked about just getting better with each game, and I think we did that today, especially with how we shared [the ball]," Howard said. "I think if we continue to play like that and continue to keep everybody on the same page, continue to move the ball, it's going to be really hard to stop us."

Added Collier: "We were moving the ball a lot. It wasn't one-on-one. We were looking for a great shot, not just a good shot, and so when we play that way, it's really fun. And I feel like our chemistry is building each game."

The U.S. will face either Spain or Australia in Saturday's semifinal, which will tip at 2 p.m. ET.

The Americans got out to a hot start, jumping ahead 36-12 at the end of the first quarter and leading 59-30 at the half. Their defense frustrated Hungary, which saw star post duo Dorka Juhasz and Virag Takacs-Kiss combine for just four points.

The U.S. had 25 of its 44 points off turnovers at the half, using defense to fuel offense on the other end.

"Everybody's just all dialed in offensively and defensively," said Angel Reese, who finished with nine points, six rebounds and three assists. "We talked about our keys, what it's going to take to win gold, and I think tonight we did everything that coach asked us to do."

Two games after Italy held the U.S. to 55 points, the Americans got mostly whatever they wanted offensively. Their 58.8% field goal percentage was their best clip of the tournament, and 12 3-pointers matched their tournament high after shooting 29% from deep in the group stage.

Team USA also won the inside battle Thursday, its 32 paint points at the half (52 overall) were more than the entire Hungary team had scored at that point.

"I feel like today was a really good one for us," Collier said. "We worked on some defensive schemes that we wanted to get better at, some offensive stuff that we wanted to clean up, and so I feel like we went out and executed that."

The 108 points marked the second most scored in a knockout game in World Cup history, behind only Brazil's 110 against the U.S. in the 1994 semifinals. The 52-point win margin was the second largest for a quarterfinal in World Cup history.

"I thought it started with our activity on the defensive end," coach Kara Lawson said. "And so our ability to turn them over, get out in transition, get some advantage plays, 2-on-1, 3-on-2, I thought gave us a lot of confidence early. And then our ability to shoot the 3-point shot ... we have a really good 3-point shooting team, and so I just thought that's what kind of jump-started us."

Lawson and the players agreed the performance was a product of their expedited chemistry-building finally starting to come into fruition. Unlike many national teams, the U.S. did not have a training camp or much prep time together before arriving in Berlin, last gathering as a group (and not its final roster) at the Final Four in April. They have now been together for about 10 days after leaving their WNBA teams.

"The more we play, the more comfortable we're getting with each other," said Young, the only American to hit double figures in each game this tournament. "And tonight we got the ball popping and we were able to get some easy buckets in transition."

Added Collier: "Today felt good, not just because of the score, but in the way that we were scoring as well."

stories.headline: NBA intel: What to expect at next week's owners' meetings
stories.summary: The next steps in the Clippers investigation, league expansion and NBA Europe could all be decided next week.
stories.body:
Adam Silver, now in his 12th year as NBA commissioner, has dealt with plenty of changes and challenges during his tenure. But Monday and Tuesday's board of governors meeting in New York represents an inflection point for the league. And his leadership will play a major role.

There are a few main agenda items that could set major events into motion that, in some cases, have been years in the making.

Most of the work by Silver and the league office has been done in the months leading up to this meeting, where the presentations and formal votes might happen, but the public rollout is a big responsibility for the commissioner, who will deliver his news conference Tuesday.

This BOG meeting has the potential to be one of more consequential ones in recent memory. Here are three topics I'm expecting Silver and the owners to discuss: the LA Clippers' investigation and punishments, NBA Europe and the next steps in expansion.

Official statements on the Clippers' salary cap circumvention punishment
Silver spoke loudly with his actions last week, slapping the Clippers with five revoked first-round draft picks and a record $30 million fine. But how he responds in front of cameras for the first time next week will set the tone going forward as this situation probably has another chapter or two to come.
The Clippers have not publicly accepted their fate or announced whether they will pursue legal action. They have not said who will act as the governor at the meeting in suspended owner Steve Ballmer's place or who will act as interim head of basketball operations in place of the suspended Lawrence Frank.

They also have not executed the trade to send Kawhi Leonard to the Toronto Raptors, a deal agreed to on the first day of free agency.

This purposeful inaction, in addition to the legal saber-rattling, can be seen as the Clippers leaving open their options and negotiation windows.

When the NBA issued its enormous penalty -- the final revoked draft pick in 2034 -- it did so knowing Ballmer might have a litigious reaction. Whether it would admit it, the league has also given itself room to negotiate. (The league and the Clippers reportedly had failed settlement discussions before the Wachtell, Lipton report was made public. )

One topic rival front offices have discussed is the less-talked-about but draconian-sounding "compliance and monitoring program by the league office for a period of five years" penalty that was also leveled on the Clippers. The terms were nebulous, probably for a reason, and the devil will surely be in the details.

"Are they going to be reading all their emails, reading their texts, listening to their phone calls?" one general manager told ESPN. "I have no idea what that [penalty] means."

The announcement of the penalty and the side deal the league cut with the players' union to have Leonard accept a $700,000 reimbursement penalty and eliminate the Clippers' option to take the NBA to arbitration, certainly changed the dynamic.

During the investigation, which spanned five major Silver news conferences, he repeatedly gave no indication of the severity of the findings, even though he said he was getting regular updates.

In the past two, before Game 1 of the 2026 Finals and after the July owners meeting in Las Vegas, Silver gave off some Judge Judy meme vibes by figuratively tapping his watch and saying the investigation needed to wrap up. It was not the posture of someone about to release a bombshell. And the Clippers, based on their public and private statements claiming shock, certainly didn't see it coming.

David Stern, Silver's legendary predecessor, was known for fiery news conferences when announcing major disciplinary actions, whether it was after the 2004 Malice at the Palace in Detroit or when he levied his own five-pick penalty to the Minnesota Timberwolves for salary cap violations in 2000. Silver is typically much more measured and disarming. When he suspended former Phoenix Suns owner Robert Sarver three years ago, Silver was even-tempered.

Soon after the report was released and the punishments announced, the Clippers issued an emotional statement and sent a seething letter to Silver. Here comes the next round.

The latest on NBA Europe -- with a possible international showdown looming
For much of the past two years, the league has been planning a major push into Europe. And recent reports have set the stage for a drama.

The Euroleague, which would be NBA Europe's main rival, is waiting for a formal offer of a partnership in the very near future and has scheduled a rare owners meeting for Oct. 5 near Lake Como in northern Italy, where it all could come to a head.

The NBA has gone through several rounds of bids and is ready to move forward with a 16-team league with 12 permanent members and four rotating members, starting in 2027. League officials have said there are bidding groups for 12 of those new teams in Europe, with franchises in London and Paris expected to go for $1 billion-plus, per league sources.

But the NBA's preference would be to blend existing Euroleague teams and new franchises into one pan-European league with NBA branding and leadership, Euroleague history and infrastructure, plus the international organization of FIBA.

That sounds nice, of course, but there's so much money and power at stake that the process to do so will be bumpy, at best.

Top officials from both the NBA and the Euroleague have said they are prepared to work together or go it alone in what surely would be an unsustainable fragmented system. It could be a seminal showdown and will be a major part of this owners meeting, multiple sources said.

The next step in NBA (domestic) expansion
The meeting could feature a vote -- or perhaps the scheduling of a vote -- to move forward with expansion, which has been long assumed but never formalized. Silver, who has said the league has been working with bankers on vetting ownership groups, could establish an exact timetable for choosing winning bids or announcing finalists.
It should not be assumed that both Las Vegas and Seattle will be on the same schedule or be close to the same price point, ownership sources said. Preliminary bidders in the $8 billion range for Vegas quickly learned the number would be higher, sources said. A Seattle team, meanwhile, could be sold for considerably less.

Some teams have been projecting the per-team payout for expansion to be $500 million to $600 million, which would put the combined expansion fee at around $15 billion to $18 billion.

Within a few months, the Los Angeles Lakers sale could close for $12.5 billion; expansion could generate a once-in-a-generation windfall for teams while also increasing their valuations; and NBA Europe might generate billions more.

With the future of those nine-, 10- and 11-figure sums potentially at stake, it's difficult to understate the importance of next week's BOG meeting for Silver and the NBA.

stories.headline: Luke Shaw to face late fitness test ahead of Manchester derby - Michael Carrick
stories.summary: Michael Carrick has said Luke Shaw will be assessed before deciding whether the defender is fit to face Manchester City.
stories.body:
Michael Carrick has said Luke Shaw will be assessed before deciding whether the defender is fit to face Manchester City.

Shaw was left out of the 4-0 win over Sabah FK on Thursday after being forced off in the 2-2 draw with Everton.

The 31-year-old started every Premier League game last season, but he's in danger of missing Sunday's Manchester derby if he cannot prove his fitness.

"We'll have to see," Carrick said.

"We just kind of looked after him a little bit. He wasn't quite ready for [Sabah] 100%, so we didn't risk it. We'll see how he is over the next couple of days or so."

City's visit to Old Trafford is a repeat of Carrick's first game in charge after taking over from Ruben Amorim on an interim basis in January.

United had gone four games without a win before the derby, but produced a stunning performance to beat City thanks to goals from Bryan Mbeumo and Patrick Dorgu.

"It'll definitely be different, just because no games are ever the same," Carrick said.

"I think there's no way we're assuming we won last year, we'll do the same things and everything will be the same.

"I think the confidence that we've built over a period of time and feel like we're getting better all the time, I think that helps us.

"We know it's a big game, we know it's an important game. There's a lot riding on it, it's pretty obvious to say, but we're looking forward to it. We've got a short space of time to recover and prepare for it, but we'll make the most of it."

Carrick was given a contract until the end of the season when he was appointed in January. Victory over City contributed to a run of 12 wins from 17 games to win the job permanently.

There was an initial expectation that United would appoint an outside candidate in the summer, but Carrick insists he was always thinking long-term.

"I think I said it pretty early on, I was always planning to be [manager beyond the summer]," he said.

"All the decisions we were making were if we were going to be here for a period of time. I never knew how long that was going to be, I still don't!

"But you're always planning for the future, what we want it to look like and the direction we want to go, and that was from day one.

"The performance the lads gave was incredible with all that, but there was definitely always -- has been, always will be for me -- from the start was planning to try and get this club to where we want to get it in the long term."
